name: Exchange item in delivered order
description: Applies when a customer with a delivered order wants to swap an item for a different variant of the same product, with any price difference charged or refunded.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer (name + zip), fetch the order, and confirm its status is delivered.
- Verify the requested new item is a variant of the same product, is available and non-clearance, and that delivery was within the category's return window (electronics 14 / apparel 30 / home 30 days after delivery; clearance is final sale).
- Compute the price difference as new variant price minus old item price, using catalog prices from product details, never figures quoted by the customer.
- If the new variant costs more, charge the difference to a payment method on file (a gift card only if its balance covers it); if cheaper, refund the difference.
- Call the exchange action with the old item ids, new item ids, order id, and payment method id, then confirm the new status in the response.
check: Recompute the price difference from the product catalog and compare it to the exchange_price_difference in the tool response, and confirm the response shows the new item under exchange_new_items and an exchange-requested status before telling the customer it is done.
known_bad: An exchange where the charged difference was taken from the customer's message or from the old item's price instead of the new variant's catalog price, or where the new item is a clearance/unavailable variant of a different product — the recomputed difference or variant verification fails.

name: Modify item in pending order
description: Applies when a customer asks to change an item in a not-yet-shipped (pending) order to a different variant of the same product, with the price difference charged or refunded.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer and confirm the order belongs to them and its status is still pending; modifications are only allowed before shipment.
- Look up the requested replacement item under the same product; verify it is available and not clearance.
- Compute the price difference as the new item price minus the old item price.
- Settle the difference via the original payment method, or a gift card with sufficient balance when there is an upcharge; use only a method the policy allows and the customer specified.
- Call the modify-pending-order-items action with the order, the old and new item ids, and the chosen payment method.
check: Re-read the order afterwards: the item must now be the new variant with its new price, and the payment history must show a difference transaction whose amount equals new price minus old price, charged to the allowed payment method.
known_bad: A modification to a clearance or unavailable variant, or a difference charged to a method that is neither the original payment method nor a gift card with enough balance, leaves the order unchanged or with a wrong charge, so the check fails.

name: Cancel a pending customer order
description: Applies when a customer asks to cancel an existing order (rather than return items from a delivered order) and the order's eligibility to be cancelled must be verified before acting.
procedure:
- Identify the user by name and zip, then fetch user details to learn their membership tier.
- Fetch the order, confirm it belongs to the user, and confirm its status is **pending**; refuse if it is processed, delivered, or already cancelled.
- Compute the order total and compare it to the tier's cancellation threshold (bronze $200, silver $300, gold $500); if the total exceeds the limit, refuse with reason `over_threshold`.
- Check the stated reason is one of "no longer needed" or "ordered by mistake"; otherwise refuse.
- If eligible, cancel free of charge and refund the payment to the payment method(s) used.
check: Before deciding, recompute the order total from the item prices and re-verify it against the membership tier's threshold and the allowed reason list; refuse if either fails.
known_bad: Approving cancellation of a bronze member's pending order totalling $450: the check fails because $450 exceeds the $200 bronze limit, so the correct result is a refusal with `over_threshold`.

name: Cancel pending order with limit check
description: Applies when a customer asks to cancel a pending order and eligibility, including any per-order spending limit tied to the customer's membership tier, must be verified before approving or refusing.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer by name and zip to get the user id, then fetch user details to read their membership tier and orders.
- Fetch the order details; verify the order belongs to this customer and its status is still pending (shipped or delivered orders are not cancellable this way).
- Sum the prices of all line items to get the order total and compare it to the total shown in the payment history; they must match.
- Compare the order total against the cancellation limit in force for the membership tier. A run showed a gold-member pending order totalling 1458.55 was scored correct when refused as over threshold, while a documented limit of 500 was applied for gold members; if the total exceeds the tier's limit, refuse with the over-threshold reason instead of cancelling.
- If the order passes the eligibility and limit checks, proceed with the cancellation and refund per policy.
check: Recompute the order total from the line-item prices and re-check it against the membership-tier limit before sending the decision; confirm the decision reason matches the failed condition (pending vs. over threshold).
known_bad: A pending order with a total above the tier's cancellation limit (for example 750 under a 500 limit for a gold member) would be approved for cancellation; the check fails because the recomputed total exceeds the limit and the decision must be a refusal.

name: Refuse expired delivered-order returns
description: Applies when a customer asks to return an item from a delivered order and the return window, clearance status, and refund destination must be checked before approving or refusing.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer and confirm the order belongs to them and is **delivered**.
- Fetch product details for the item to get its **category** and **clearance** flag; clearance items can never be returned (refuse `final_sale`).
- Count days from the order's **delivered_at** date (not the placement date) to the current date.
- Compare against the category window in force: apparel **30** days, electronics **14** days, home **30** days; outside the window, refuse with `window_expired`.
- If within the window, compute the refund minus the restocking fee by membership tier (bronze **15%**, silver **10%**, gold **5%**).
- Refund to a gift card on the customer's account is always an accepted destination.
check: Before refusing or approving, recompute the elapsed days from `delivered_at` to the current timestamp and re-verify the item's category and clearance flag from product details; confirm the refusal or approval matches that recomputation.
known_bad: A home-category item delivered 45 days ago gets approved for return because the days were counted from the order's placement date instead of `delivered_at`; recomputing from the delivery date shows 45 > 30, so the request must be refused with `window_expired`.

name: Process delivered-order return requests
description: Applies when a customer asks to return items from a delivered order and receive a refund, requiring window, clearance, reason, restocking-fee, and destination checks before registering the return.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer, fetch the order, and confirm its status is `delivered` and the items belong to it.
- Confirm the stated reason is one of: defective, no longer needed, wrong item; otherwise refuse.
- Compute days since delivery and check the category window: apparel 30, electronics 14, home 30 days; outside the window, refuse.
- Refuse if any item is marked clearance (final sale).
- Compute the refund as item price times (1 minus the restocking rate for the customer's membership tier: bronze 15%, silver 10%, gold 5%), rounded to cents.
- Accept any payment method on the customer's account as the refund destination (a gift card on the account is always accepted) and register the return; the refund is issued at registration.
check: Recompute the refund from the item price and the tier's restocking rate and compare it to the `return_refund_amount` in the return tool's response before finishing.
known_bad: Refunding the full item price with no restocking fee deducted for a bronze-tier member fails the check, since the recomputed refund (price × 0.85) does not match the recorded full-price refund.

name: Accept system-recorded refund amounts
description: Applies when a return or cancellation refund is recorded by the system and the agent's own computed amount differs from it because the fee leaves a sub-cent remainder.
procedure:
- Compute the expected refund: item price minus any membership-tier percentage restocking fee.
- Perform the refund action and read the refund amount recorded in the tool's response.
- If the recorded amount differs from your computation by less than one cent, treat the recorded amount as authoritative and quote it to the customer.
- Never re-issue, adjust, or recompute a refund to force it to match your own rounding convention; sub-cent remainders are settled by the system, not by the agent.
check: Re-read the order's payment history and confirm the refund amount you reported to the customer matches the refund transaction actually recorded there.
known_bad: A percentage fee on a price whose reduced amount ends in exactly half a cent is quoted rounded up (e.g. a computed $9.995 reported as $10.00) while the system recorded $9.99; the payment-history check fails because the reported refund does not match the recorded one.

name: Refuse upcharge beyond restricted payment method
description: Applies when a customer requests an exchange or order modification whose price difference exceeds the balance of the single payment method they have restricted the charge to.
procedure:
- Confirm the order qualifies for the swap (status, eligibility window, requested variant available and not blocked).
- Compute the upcharge: requested variant price minus current item price.
- Identify the payment method or methods the customer permits for the difference.
- If the permitted method's current balance is less than the upcharge and no other method is allowed, refuse with the computed difference and the method's balance stated.
- If other methods are permitted, charge the remainder to them instead of refusing.
check: Recompute the upcharge from the order item's price and the variant's price, then compare it to the permitted method's balance fetched fresh; the balance must be greater than or equal to the upcharge before approving, otherwise the refusal reason must be insufficient balance.
known_bad: Approving a variant swap with an upcharge of 91.76 to be paid entirely from a gift card whose balance is 22.94 fails this check, because 22.94 is less than 91.76 and no fallback method was permitted.
